characters.imageAlt: Discord depiction of Quoth

characters.title: Vaemyr
characters.meta: Tiefling wizard; diplomat and consequence-minded protector
characters.summary: Vaemyr thinks carefully, admits uncertainty, determines what he owes, and then commits without holding part of himself in reserve.

characters.title: Krone
characters.summary: A joyous front-line protector whose primordial strength and loyalty carry him from Pristinia and Gael into the battle against Wrath.

characters.title: Saylor
characters.summary: A priestess and expedition member whose quest history includes the Hin crisis, Voraketh, and repeated rescue attempts.
characters.imageAlt: Discord depiction of Saylor

characters.title: Navi
characters.summary: A recurring adventurer in late-2024 and 2025 quest arcs, often traveling with Sparrow, Stormy, and Amity.
characters.imageAlt: Navi with green eyes, black and green hair, and a pointed ear

characters.title: Loistava
characters.summary: An early Pristinia defender, Eovar investigator, voyager, and witness to the doppelganger return.
characters.imageAlt: Loistava with white hair, pointed ears and pale blue armor

characters.title: Trougar
characters.summary: Joins the old-road expedition, finds a carving and watches a shadow child at Viota’s monument.
characters.imageAlt: Discord depiction of Trougar

characters.title: Lucido Spettoro
characters.summary: An explorer and chronicler who asks what adventuring changes for a community, then carries the memory of earlier journeys into later choices.
characters.imageAlt: Lucido Spettoro in a monochrome portrait with dark hair, a beard and a fur-lined collar

characters.title: Erebus Duskforge
characters.summary: A recurring player-controlled adventurer in the 2025 quest record.
characters.imageAlt: Erebus with a dark beard and braided hair, surrounded by glowing magic

characters.title: Oya
characters.summary: A frequently played adventurer whose later campaign record crosses expeditions and community scenes.
characters.imageAlt: Oya with blue skin and hair, a pale pointed hat and a blue staff

characters.title: Willow
characters.summary: A recurring Pristinia adventurer tied to harvest defense, Hin expeditions, festivals, and later journeys.
characters.imageAlt: Discord depiction of Willow

characters.title: Leo
characters.summary: An explorer active in the sector dungeon, quarry mission, Rehevä crisis, and early Delerium investigations.
characters.imageAlt: Leo with silver hair and blue eyes, reading an open book amid blue lightning

characters.title: Cobble
characters.summary: An early Pristinia defender, militia trainer, ruin explorer, and witness to the town’s first hidden threats.

characters.title: Bitoshi Nakamoto
characters.meta: Adventurer · loyalty, grief and chosen bonds
characters.summary: An explorer whose loyalty persists through Jiangshi’s absence and return, Adelia’s grief, and the difficult work of remaining beside people after catastrophe.

characters.title: Fulmin
characters.summary: A repeatedly controlled adventurer with a substantial later-archive presence.
characters.imageAlt: Fulmin in armor with blue lightning and a long weapon

characters.title: Empty
characters.summary: A player-controlled explorer involved in the sector dungeon, Delerium sites, and Pristinia’s early contamination crisis.
characters.imageAlt: Empty with spiked dark hair and black and red clothing against a dark red background

characters.title: Elysian ‘Eli’ Voss
characters.summary: A musician-adventurer active in Pristinia’s defense, festivals, and late-2024 expeditions.
characters.imageAlt: Eli Voss wearing a green hood and carrying a sword in a town street

characters.title: Vigr Frami
characters.summary: An early militia organizer and defender who helped recover the mine dead and negotiate Pristinia’s wolf pact.
characters.imageAlt: Discord depiction of Vigr Frami

characters.title: Tricks
characters.summary: An investigator and field adventurer tied to Eovar, Nienna’s rescue, and The Before’s early crises.
characters.imageAlt: Discord depiction of Tricks

characters.title: Dorian Ashwood
characters.summary: A caravan musician whose friendship, grief and care repeatedly confront him with the difference between protecting someone and forcing an answer.
characters.imageAlt: Dorian Ashwood with brown hair and a stringed instrument over his shoulder

characters.title: Rolen Ofandrus
characters.summary: Rolen makes protection practical: equipment prepared by hand, newcomers taught patiently and a range made useful to the town.
characters.imageAlt: Rolen with pointed ears and armor, carrying swords

characters.title: Spicy
characters.summary: A recurring player-controlled adventurer in the quest archive.
characters.imageAlt: Discord depiction of Spicy

characters.title: Oleander
characters.summary: A recurring player-controlled adventurer in the later quest archive.
characters.imageAlt: Oleander holding a staff amid golden paper birds

characters.title: Yllandaer
characters.summary: A recurring adventurer active in Pristinia investigations and 2025 expeditions.
characters.imageAlt: Discord depiction of Yllandaer

characters.title: Nerias
characters.summary: An adventurer present from Pristinia’s first ritual-site defense through later investigations and journeys.
characters.imageAlt: Nerias as a horned warrior carrying an ornate shield and sword

characters.title: Rory
characters.summary: A recurring player-controlled adventurer in the later campaign record.
characters.imageAlt: Rory with purple hair, dark lipstick and silver jewelry

characters.title: Eldin Stormheart
characters.summary: A recurring adventurer associated with Pristinia’s late-2024 and 2025 quests.
characters.imageAlt: Eldin with long blond hair, a beard and a dark fur-lined cloak

characters.title: Paw
characters.summary: An adventurer active in redcap recovery, Hin expeditions, and later Pristinia scenes.
characters.imageAlt: Paw as a dark bear with glowing red eyes in a forest

characters.title: Stormy
characters.summary: A recurring adventurer often traveling with Navi, Sparrow, and Amity.
characters.imageAlt: Discord depiction of Stormy

characters.title: Kasiri Ruza
characters.summary: A craftswoman and curious investigator who turns interdependence, honest limits and Pristinia’s civic memory into practical responsibility.
characters.imageAlt: Kasiri with silver hair, freckles and layered armor

characters.title: Bari
characters.summary: An early explorer of Eovar, Rehevä, the sector dungeon, and Pristinia’s civic life.
characters.imageAlt: Bari with pale hair in a close-up portrait

characters.title: Karnak
characters.summary: An earnest protector who seeks to prove conviction through action while learning to decide alongside stronger companions.
characters.imageAlt: Karnak surrounded by golden light, carrying a large golden weapon

characters.title: Gudlaug
characters.summary: A field adventurer and public-race champion active in the 2024 quest record.
characters.imageAlt: Gudlaug in dark armor carrying a sword in a snowy landscape

characters.title: Alfred Riverheart
characters.summary: Voraketh explorer who damages a Chain, later dies and returns through an unidentified voice at the Last Grove as unnatural spores erupt.

characters.title: Camilla Blackwood
characters.summary: An institution-builder whose educational work and security concerns remain part of a history that later includes relinquishing her Order.

characters.title: St. Anky
characters.summary: Nuru’s saint and sharing knight; builds the Temple’s surviving record before a chain-guard construct kills him and Alfred on 20 April 2026.

characters.title: Draygar WarSmash
characters.summary: A rescuer, sworn brother, and front-line protector whose great strength matters most when it carries another person out of danger.

characters.title: Eugene
characters.meta: Player character · scholar and reluctant bearer
characters.summary: Names himself as a burden immediately before asking the useful question or carrying difficult knowledge.

characters.title: Gregory Greenleaf
characters.summary: Challenges Ale-Chemy financing, helps rescue a child from Krampus, and accompanies Farkur to the graves.

characters.title: Lichen
characters.summary: A visibly strange newcomer who learns that Skye can be a safe friend.
characters.imageAlt: Lichen with leaf-like hair, a pink flower and bright green butterflies

characters.title: Miri
characters.summary: Joins the Pristinian–Rahuvian survey of The Before and helps carry its recovered evidence forward.

characters.title: Adelia & Hope
characters.summary: Love confronts loss through shadow, mercy and sacrifice. Bound to Hope and Gael, Adelia must still face the boundaries of protection.

characters.title: Akarian Irenhour
characters.summary: Akarian Irenhour: hunter, witness and Guardian of Gael, preserving heritage while training and protecting companions.

characters.title: Alesteir
characters.summary: A player character whose portrait is now correctly assigned; older spelling variants remain searchable.

characters.title: Aravil
characters.summary: Recognizes comrades by shared battles, admits error without surrendering competence, and returns when war becomes consequential.

characters.title: Arjahn
characters.summary: A disciplined protector who plans routes home and makes other people’s solutions stronger.

characters.title: Brianna
characters.summary: A druid whose experience of repeated death shapes a difficult commitment to life, freedom and trial amid the Rahu war, and whose grief finds an outlet in useful service.

characters.title: Cecil
characters.summary: A careful observer remembered for attention to individual vines and leaves; travels through time with Olokun.

characters.title: Carmen
characters.summary: A deep gnome warlock whose ledger of obligation is tested by Paco’s unchosen sacrifice.

characters.title: Coralyn
characters.summary: A sea-minded explorer whose desire to unite people develops alongside a disciplined refusal to join mysteries before the evidence supports it.

characters.title: Dale
characters.meta: Centaur musician; protector and reluctant leader
characters.summary: Dale makes life inside catastrophe funny, familiar, and worth protecting; his simple loyalty gives ordinary affection the weight of history.

characters.title: Dez
characters.summary: A tavern-scene presence who repeatedly opens conversational space for Ghilsen and Magnus.
characters.imageAlt: Dez wearing a hood and crouching on a rooftop lantern at sunset

characters.title: Elenia
characters.summary: A bearer of light whose devotion does not require moral blindness.

characters.title: Gartina
characters.summary: A chef and protector for whom preparation is care—and can become self-blame.

characters.title: Farkur
characters.summary: Turns hospitality, specialized labor, shared tools, and funding into an institution intended to outlast any one adventurer.

characters.title: Ghilsen Hendrickson
characters.summary: A formerly enslaved adventurer whose freedom, marriage and return from death remain personal histories rather than a completed heroic legend.

characters.title: Ithilrûnë Ailinor
characters.summary: A researcher whose commitment to memory and independent judgment meets its hardest test when understanding itself fails.

characters.title: Jéane Rose
characters.summary: Experiences thought, friendship, travel, and the obligation to protect at extraordinary speed.

characters.title: Jiangshi
characters.summary: Returned from prolonged death, Jiangshi trusts the continuity of ancestors, family and chosen love. Her shadows can shelter and heal; her care remains present even when gods, factions and a resurrected friend fail.
characters.imageAlt: Jiangshi in dark robes holding a decorated fan beneath pale blossoms

characters.title: Magnus Niriin
characters.summary: A Prima adventurer turned Rahu operative whose pursuit of leverage later carries him into Zarathian politics and deepening dependence on Death.

characters.title: Minerva
characters.summary: A persistent investigator who turns inherited knowledge into field practice while testing how much risk research can ask others to bear.

characters.title: Nienna
characters.summary: Elenia restores her after a first death in Gael; her later sacrifice for Hope continues to shape the living.

characters.title: Nymera
characters.meta: Cala devotee · civic worker and expedition ally
characters.summary: A Cala devotee who finds purpose and relief in practical work, even while unsure what she wants beyond being useful.

characters.title: Olokun
characters.summary: A deeply attached protector whose mature ethic separates care from ownership while fear keeps testing that boundary.

characters.title: Pappy
characters.summary: A simple, good man whose Rift rescue exposes the boundary between character knowledge and later governance disputes.

characters.title: Quake
characters.summary: A first-wave adventurer whose scouting, rescue work, civic labor, and battlefield resolve help turn Pristinia into a defensible home.

characters.title: Saray
characters.summary: An archer whose work in Gael joins anger, grief, love and the continued defense of her companions; she lands the final blow against Wrath.

characters.title: Rahn
characters.summary: A player-character pet recorded flying and scouting with the adventuring company. The owner is not identified here.
characters.imageAlt: Rahn as a brown vulture perched on a rock

characters.title: Ryvyt
characters.meta: Main member of the Ale-Chemy Knights
characters.summary: A founder and lead crafter whose work turns shared resources into useful equipment, while later discoveries preserve the history of those who handled them before him.

characters.title: Scribonia
characters.summary: Self-defined before every label; named by several early voters as a possible custodian of Papirak’s staff, though the vote remains unresolved.

characters.title: Selwyn
characters.summary: A player character preserved in the recovered catalogue.
characters.imageAlt: Discord depiction of Selwyn

characters.title: Lady Severina Blackveil
characters.meta: Player character · Veilguard leader and civic defender
characters.summary: A commander whose authority grows through peer trust, practical protection and decisions that must answer to evidence.

characters.title: Sildithas
characters.summary: Meets uncertain divine authority by returning to an oath of mercy, flourishing, courage, and preserved joy.

characters.title: Swift Foot
characters.meta: Harengon ranger · scout and contested martyr
characters.summary: Quick with a bow and a joke, Swift Foot argues for ordinary people’s freedom and leaves a contested legacy after his final stand against Rahu authority.
characters.imageAlt: Discord depiction of Swift Foot

characters.title: Thorn
characters.summary: A Veilguard member whose healing, field investigation and rebuilding continue after death and a hard-won recovery in Gael.

characters.title: Tobias Goodbarrel
characters.summary: A halfling builder and main Ale-Chemy Knight who gives strangers safety, practical knowledge and the freedom to choose how they will belong.
characters.imageAlt: Tobias, a stout halfling with a shaved head and dark beard, wearing ornate armor and a green cloak

characters.title: Tshuka Hayim
characters.summary: A traveler whose remembered rules of the Shadow Roads coexist with curiosity, practical aid and a growing place in local memory.

characters.title: Vaelith
characters.summary: A player character preserved in the recovered catalogue.

characters.title: Wren
characters.summary: Feels what history costs individual people and keeps helping inside grief, even when responsibility threatens to consume her.

characters.title: Alioth
characters.summary: A reader who turns curiosity into expeditions, approaches institutions through conversation and chooses loyalty to Casimir even when it costs admission to the Rahu.
characters.imageAlt: Alioth with dark hair, blue armor and blue gemstone jewelry

characters.title: Aurélia / Night
characters.summary: A Magic Academy student who favors Scribonia as custodian of Papirak’s staff while voicing discomfort with taking the object from him.

characters.title: Casimir
characters.summary: A questioning adventurer whose procedural reasoning and loyalty to Alioth expose the difference between understanding an institution and giving it first claim.

characters.title: Di’Trillio
characters.meta: Seeker · explorer and advocate for the Dasa
characters.summary: Survives the haze, helps investigate the harpy cave and later promises Kimi and Kuri that he will find Vey and Vaa.

characters.title: Djöhandrai
characters.summary: Djo hides, stammers and loves a good meal—and keeps choosing to help people in danger.

characters.title: Fenwick d'Jorasco
characters.summary: Founder of Vital Chain, healer and investigator of Eovar: Fenwick turns knowledge into public work, healing networks and magical routes, while his hunger for understanding carries its own dangers.
characters.imageAlt: Fenwick d’Jorasco, wearing round glasses and a green cloak, holding a glowing spell

characters.title: Marius Antares
characters.summary: Observes changes in Prima and voices a belief about Gael’s economy that remains attributed rather than established.
characters.imageAlt: Marius Antares with brown hair, green eyes and a dark coat

characters.title: Moira Eshdin
characters.summary: Questions the origins of cave contamination, aids Pell when he falls and accepts uncertainty about the fragments’ spread.
characters.imageAlt: Moira Eshdin with short dark hair and an eyepatch, seated at a table

characters.title: Pelegia
characters.summary: Urges retreat from Hana’s tower and returns with Ryvyt to question market residents about the forest. Insists on burial in the harpy cave, helps gather Tabitha’s ingredients and gains purpose through trusted service at Papirak’s funeral. An adventurer who introduces himself to the company, stays close to Carmen and offers healing after a fight.

characters.title: Saoirse
characters.summary: Heals Vessalia, helps close the harpy cave and states an intention to educate Pristinia’s young.

characters.title: Vessalia
characters.summary: A high elf bard finding companions, confronting the dangers of adventuring, and building a home with Di’trillio near the Lily Patch.

characters.title: Animak
characters.summary: A hesitant arrival whose strange lantern makes Arjahn’s first offer of help unexpectedly complicated.
characters.imageAlt: Animak, a cloaked figure carrying a glowing lantern near a distant lighthouse

characters.title: Krasteline
characters.summary: A crafter who investigates the Gate, helps Fenwick to his feet and tries to keep her companions looking forward.
characters.imageAlt: Krasteline with blue skin, orange hair and illuminated goggles

characters.title: Goo
characters.summary: A newcomer whose unfamiliar form briefly alarms Vaemyr before conversation restores the welcome.
characters.imageAlt: Goo depicted as a blue translucent figure

characters.title: Icarus
characters.summary: A frightened arrival whose chicken disguise lets him survive a Rahu search party.
characters.imageAlt: Icarus as a robed rooster figure surrounded by chickens

characters.title: Starojoss Destranoth
characters.summary: Star writes down the strange parts of a story before anyone can make them tidier than they were.
characters.imageAlt: Discord depiction of Starojoss Destranoth

characters.title: Saelihn
characters.meta: Player character · psionic helper and careful explorer
characters.summary: A companion who supports the Common Man’s rebuilding and protects the living growth around Viota’s monument.
characters.imageAlt: Recorded depiction of Saelihn

characters.title: Fredrick
characters.summary: An adventurer whose place in the grimoire’s custody history gives a seemingly unreadable possession consequences beyond his lifetime.

characters.title: Aerrow
characters.summary: A scout who seeks freedom through strength, learns the cost of overreaching in Babel’s wilds and helps turn dangerous journeys into supplies for the Refuge.
characters.imageAlt: Aerrow with long pale hair, a dark cloak and a large sword

scenes.title: Aerrow · Moving portrait
scenes.caption: Aerrow with pale hair and glowing violet eyes, framed by flames and sparks. Supplied moving portrait.

npcs.title: Papirak the Strange
npcs.meta: NPC · archmage and Training Dungeon teacher
npcs.summary: A Pristinian wizard formally entombed beside his Training Dungeon, with his Staff of Power buried under Sequester and his unfinished institutions inherited by the living.

prominence.reason: The established Papirak chronology links teaching and lasting civic institutions.

npcs.imageAlt: Papirak with long pale hair and a beard, holding a glowing blue orb

npcs.title: Melian Starguard
npcs.summary: A civic authority who carries Pristinia through siege, abduction, return, and remembrance without treating extraordinary power as a substitute for public responsibility.

prominence.reason: The user confirms this label belongs to Pristinia’s established civic leader.

npcs.title: Poe
npcs.summary: Administers the public vote on Papirak’s Staff of Power, making procedure and recordkeeping active forces in Pristinia’s history.
npcs.imageAlt: Poe with dark hair and round glasses, writing with a luminous feather quill

npcs.title: Aria / Pride
npcs.summary: A daughter of Death whose philosophy treats attachment as future weakness.

npcs.title: Vain
npcs.summary: Death’s most trusted Knight according to Aionia, hunting Shards for the Wyrm and seeking divine grace.

npcs.title: High Lord Bowene
npcs.summary: High Lord before Aria’s death; his civic office is distinct from her cultural leadership.

npcs.title: Endora
npcs.summary: A woman whose choices are repeatedly filtered through the people who tried to keep or preserve her.

npcs.title: Alessio
npcs.summary: Works the tables, cleans mugs, and makes the tavern legible as a civilian workplace.
npcs.imageAlt: Alessio with pink hair, green eyes and dark ornamental jewelry

npcs.title: Farmer Frank
npcs.summary: Carries the ordinary cost when promised harvest help does not return.

prominence.reason: The existing public record preserves civilian cost and obligations toward farming.

npcs.imageAlt: Farmer Frank carrying an axe over his shoulder beside fields

npcs.title: Herb Shepard
npcs.meta: Common Man owner and barkeeper · Pristinia
npcs.summary: Also recorded as Herb Sheperd / Shepherd. Welcomes newcomers, safeguards supplies and survives to help clear the Common Man’s ruins.
npcs.imageAlt: Herb seated in a tavern, holding a mug

npcs.title: Paco
npcs.summary: His sacrifice turns obligation into a question about love, choice, and ownership.
npcs.imageAlt: Paco with purple coloring, long pointed ears and yellow eyes

npcs.title: Roderick / Wrath
npcs.summary: A duke and Knight whose history reaches the players in consequential fragments.

npcs.title: Serra
npcs.summary: A tavern worker whose observation about declining tips preserves the civilian economic effect of an adventurer’s absence.

prominence.reason: Hospitality and local relationships give the Common Man continuity.

npcs.title: Skye
npcs.summary: Refuses to exploit Lichen’s generosity and connects a newcomer to the First Forest through music and conversation.

prominence.reason: Music and care contribute to the Common Man’s public social life.

npcs.title: The Liar
npcs.summary: Trades Delerium to Roderick for Eldrin’s relic, enabling Endora’s corrupted return.

npcs.title: Tutora Rhex
npcs.summary: Carries Elenia home from the Liar’s prison and preserves a source account of the Delerium trade.

npcs.title: Vysaeth
npcs.summary: A ruler whose testimony becomes an early lens on Roderick and Endora.

npcs.title: Commander Yvette
npcs.summary: A commander whose lifetime of service, wary dealings with visitors and grief for her soldiers give her corps a history of its own.

npcs.title: Witch Queen Ephraith
npcs.summary: A ruler whose fierce defense of Rahu interests can sustain collective grievance—and whose willingness to revise judgment makes restitution and peace possible.

npcs.title: Scout Lilian
npcs.summary: A field guide and early-warning coordinator killed by Rahu archers on Magnus’s direct order while attempting to warn Pristinia.

prominence.reason: Warnings, scouting infrastructure and the cost of her loss shape Pristinia’s history.

npcs.title: Strange Talon
npcs.summary: An Owlin intelligence chief whose conditional hospitality becomes a lasting grievance against the adventurers he believes escaped Rahu justice.

npcs.title: Ambassador Sophina
npcs.summary: The polished diplomatic voice of Rahu interests: willing to bargain and cooperate while defending the law and sovereignty of her own people.
npcs.imageAlt: Sophina in dark robes holding a sheathed sword beneath a red and white moon

npcs.title: Huoth, Emissary of Nuru
npcs.meta: Angel of Nuru · caretaker of Gael
npcs.summary: The guardian who kept Gael’s last sanctuary alive until mortals could carry its watch—and whose angelic nature was revealed after his physical service ended.
npcs.imageAlt: Huoth in an ornate dark hood with luminous markings beneath his eyes

npcs.title: Yami no Majo
npcs.meta: Venerable Rahu mage and cultural intermediary
npcs.summary: A respected mage who explains what Rahu membership permits—and whose quiet fan gestures reveal the labor beneath Rahu refinement.

prominence.reason: The public teacher dossier connects Rahu institutions and the people learning within them.

npcs.imageAlt: Discord depiction of Yami no Majo

npcs.title: The Dragonsisters
npcs.meta: Zarathian Dragonborn sisters and deep-cover agents
npcs.summary: Sheeva, Kaiya, and Minyah spent five years out of sight; Zarathis brought their service into the light, then each chose a different life after the war.

npcs.title: Sheeva Dragonsister
npcs.meta: Zarathian operative, honored lady, and painter
npcs.summary: A soldierly intelligence operative whose public service, painting, and growing trust in Eugene preserve different parts of her life after war.

prominence.reason: Her existing public dossier provides a regional institutional and relational role.

npcs.title: Kaiya Dragonsister
npcs.summary: Patient and cautious, Kaiya turns the instincts of a long-hidden operative toward the poorly documented origins of her own people.

prominence.reason: Her existing public dossier connects scholarship with Zarathian institutions.

npcs.imageAlt: Kaiya with pale hair wearing dark armor and a pointed mask with blue glowing eyes

npcs.title: Minyah Dragonsister
npcs.summary: Public honor changes Minyah’s status, but she still calls herself a lowly spy and looks toward the next mission.

prominence.reason: Her existing public dossier provides an enduring regional operative role.

npcs.imageAlt: Minyah with long pale hair, horn-like adornments and dark armor, carrying a sword

npcs.title: Captain Hildethrax
npcs.summary: Second rank, guarded archives, investigations, and supply routes: the practical work behind Rahu authority.
npcs.imageAlt: Hildethrax in a monochrome portrait wearing a dark coat and chains

npcs.title: Deyara Thorn
npcs.summary: Physisia names Deyara Thorne as a former leader and asks Pappy to find her. Her whereabouts and the anomaly surrounding her name remain unresolved.

npcs.title: Murr the Old Wolf
npcs.meta: Voraketh wolf, guide, and surviving witness
npcs.summary: An old wolf who knows the island’s paths and remembers an earlier world, while Voraketh erodes the memories she carries.
npcs.imageAlt: Murr, a pale wolf walking along a forest path

npcs.title: Kvethe
npcs.summary: A defender of Babel’s remaining people who balances secrecy, ecological knowledge, and a refusal to abandon her home.
npcs.imageAlt: Kvethe in a forest, with dark hair and feathered adornments

npcs.title: Quille
npcs.summary: A young survivor carrying the weight of interrupted succession, hunger, and the daily work of keeping her people alive.
npcs.imageAlt: Quille with braided dark hair, pointed ears, beads and a pale shawl

npcs.title: Omari
npcs.summary: A young voice preserving Babel’s stories while carefully distinguishing what the elders taught from what Omari has seen.
npcs.imageAlt: Omari with short dark hair, facial scars and a green cloak

npcs.title: Kyrin the Lost
npcs.meta: Freed captive · witness to lost Babel
npcs.summary: A survivor of petrification whose fragmented memories preserve a beautiful land and the pain of its loss.
npcs.imageAlt: Kyrin with blue skin, horns and a gold forehead ornament

npcs.title: Rhea
npcs.summary: A named participant in the survivors’ campfire whose individual history remains largely unrecovered.
npcs.imageAlt: Rhea with short brown hair, carrying a bow, arrows and a pack

npcs.title: Neemah
npcs.summary: A bark-skinned figure who greets newcomers with a call to work for life, whether by blade, hammer, pen or scroll.

prominence.reason: A brief but distinctive presence in the recorded arrivals; wider consequences remain limited.

npcs.imageAlt: Neemah with textured dark skin and a bright blue forehead marking in the rain

npcs.title: Tarwen of the Silver Star
npcs.meta: Silver Star host in Fein Uaill
npcs.summary: The host who welcomes the company to its castle and presents mortal ascension as a shared ambition.

prominence.reason: A durable regional host and relationship figure in the existing public dossier.

npcs.imageAlt: Discord depiction of Tarwen of the Silver Star

npcs.title: Kumai-218
npcs.summary: An ancient warforged whose trials join combat, judgment and teamwork across the earliest Pristinian training and the new vanguard’s formation.

npcs.title: Farmer Scarlett
npcs.summary: A Pristinian civilian whose wartime work makes survival a matter of water, bedding, labor and space.
npcs.imageAlt: Farmer Scarlett wearing a straw hat and blue overalls in a sunlit field

npcs.title: Hana
npcs.summary: A name associated with the tower near Larkhollow, a small doll and a dangerous larger presence whose relationship remains unclear.
npcs.imageAlt: Hana with pale hair carrying a flower basket along a woodland path

npcs.title: Mama Tabitha
npcs.summary: A forest herbalist who calls for help gathering rare ingredients when ordinary remedies fail her husband.
npcs.imageAlt: Mama Tabitha pouring liquid into a bottle with a small companion beside her

npcs.title: Kazhinju
npcs.summary: A witch whose possessive claim over Bogdan turns an ingredient-gathering mission into violence, confession and a chance to help him.
npcs.imageAlt: Kazhinju with long gray hair, a tooth-adorned headband and a carved wooden staff

npcs.title: Hawthorne
npcs.summary: The scribe who turns Pristinia’s arguments into counted votes, recorded decisions and an institutional memory.

npcs.title: Vizsla, the Florist
npcs.summary: A flower-shop owner who argues that adventurers’ contributions should be recognized without displacing the settlement’s residents.

prominence.reason: Trade and civilian representation link everyday work to governance.

npcs.imageAlt: Discord depiction of Vizsla, the Florist

npcs.title: Stella & Sola

islands.title: Fenumion & the Void
islands.summary: Inhabited lands survive as separated pockets around the enormous, branching geographic and cosmological Void.

islands.title: The Void
islands.summary: The dangerous space between shattered lands: barrier, predator-space, knowledge boundary, moral problem, and changing measure of connection.

islands.title: Prima
islands.summary: The island of Prima connects Eovar Harbor and the Thundering Coast with Pristinia, the Gate, the Before and the island’s other named landscapes. Pristinia and Eovar retain separate settlement maps.

islands.title: Fein Uaill
islands.summary: The wider Zarathian region containing cities, estates, sacred sites, walls, libraries, and shores.

islands.title: Gael
islands.summary: A land where each generation inherits the work of keeping Death’s victory reversed: refuge, restoration, renewed loss and the choice to rebuild again.

islands.title: Eovar Harbor
islands.summary: A dense, defended port of roughly two thousand people, shaped by shipping and controlled water access.

islands.title: Babel-Ashur
islands.summary: An enormous island defined by wild biomes and a vast central wound rather than one dominant city.

islands.title: Voraketh
islands.summary: An island of unnatural order, old Chains, a memory-taking Wasteland, a growing Maw, and deliberately unresolved relationships.

islands.title: The Maw
islands.summary: A growing anomaly that exerts deadly pull, consumes magic, and contains or is associated with an unidentified figure.

islands.title: The Chains
islands.summary: Whale-sized antimagic structures attributed to Talan; reportedly good at first and now a curse.
islands.source: Direct observation + Nuru → Anky + Physisia → Pappy → Anky

islands.title: The Wasteland
islands.summary: Land beyond the Chains where creatures roam, magic becomes unreliable, motes can be found, and parts of a person may be lost.

islands.title: The Last Grove
islands.summary: Physisia’s last foothold in Voraketh: a living refuge of weathered stone, costly communion and a forest threatened by devouring and spores.

islands.title: Temple of Secrets
islands.summary: Anky’s protected repository for secrets, scrolls, theories, and communal gear—built so knowledge could survive the island’s losses.

islands.title: Veiled Watch
islands.meta: Voraketh · Expedition planning and record context
islands.summary: Voraketh’s operational research context, where maps, shared theories and expedition plans precede Anky’s fatal encounter at the Binding Chains.

islands.title: The Road
islands.summary: An unsafe, mostly abandoned route toward the Plains of Trial and Gael’s interior, passing monuments of an incompletely recovered past.

islands.title: Mage’s Ruin

islands.imageCaption: Gael. Mage’s Ruin, illustrated at the opening of its roleplay post.

islands.title: Vysaeth’s Tomb

islands.title: Citadel of Sorrow

islands.title: Plains of Trial

islands.title: Underwater Temple

islands.title: Zarathis

islands.title: Caisleán na Brón
islands.meta: Fein Uaill · adventurers’ stronghold and refuge

islands.title: Ciaránach

islands.title: Holy Road to Ciaránach

islands.title: Temple in Ciaránach

islands.title: Gates of Aelthor

islands.imageCaption: The opening Gates of Aelthor description and guide’s mighty-bridge dialogue directly identify the outpost approach. The guide also spells its name Aethlor; do not silently resolve that variation.

islands.title: Seraphis
islands.summary: A major settlement confirmed by the Fein Uaill map and supplied screenshot directory.
islands.imageCaption: Opening post identifies Seraphis as the holy city on a hill above Zarathis; the following guide explicitly points it out.

islands.title: The Titanwall of Eryndor

islands.imageCaption: This image is attached to the opening description identifying the Titanwall as the dam city controlling the river.

islands.title: The Shard of Fein Uaill

islands.title: The Radiant Bazaar of Zarathis
islands.summary: A Zarathian market confirmed by the supplied screenshot directory.

islands.title: Niriin Estate

islands.imageCaption: Magnus leads Eldin down an extravagant hallway toward the estate’s dining room; this image is attached to that movement.

islands.title: Aria’s Tomb
islands.summary: Aria’s tomb lies in Fein Uaill proper; the regional record corrects the assumption that it is inside Ciaránach.

islands.title: The Shining Shores

islands.title: Thalanbor the Boundless Artwright’s Library
islands.summary: A monumental library confirmed by the location directory and a supplied moving visual record.

islands.title: The Feytouched Forest
islands.summary: A named forest confirmed by the supplied screenshot directory.
islands.imageCaption: Image is attached to the opening description naming the true wilds of Fein Uaill and the Verdant Circle’s sacred forest.

islands.title: Eshnunna of the Eternal Flame
islands.summary: The inner citadel reached beyond Ciaránach’s streets, with a distinct threshold within the pilgrimage.

islands.title: Mineral Rock Face

islands.title: Unmarked Ruins

islands.title: Sulphuric Swamps

interactiveMaps.title: World
interactiveMaps.alt: Illustrated world map of Fenumion, showing separated lands around the branching Void
interactiveMaps.description: The surviving world map places the recovered lands around the Void. Several landmasses remain unnamed or only partially documented.

interactiveMaps.title: Prima
interactiveMaps.alt: Map of Prima showing Eovar Harbor, the Thundering Coast, Pristinia, the Gate, the Before, Old Earth Hills, the First Forest, Kinich Ahau, the Rahu, Lost Shacks and the Shard
interactiveMaps.description: The island of Prima connects Eovar Harbor and the Thundering Coast with Pristinia, the Gate, the Before and the island’s other named landscapes. Pristinia and Eovar retain separate settlement maps.

pins.title: The Before
pins.summary: The Before lies in northeastern Prima. Its public survey history follows the expedition into its ruins; the island marker does not locate the survey entrance precisely.

interactiveMaps.title: Pristinia
interactiveMaps.alt: Annotated civic map of Pristinia with walls, homes, businesses, temples, and public spaces
interactiveMaps.description: A civic map of accumulated ordinary life: defenses, trade, worship, food, learning, and the tavern that became a vessel for communal memory.

interactiveMaps.title: Gael
interactiveMaps.alt: Regional map of Gael showing Hope, ruins, the Plains of Trial, tombs, a tower, and an underwater temple
interactiveMaps.description: Gael’s map makes recovery visible against the scale of catastrophe: Hope is a small green foothold among ruins, trials, tombs, and old strongholds.

interactiveMaps.title: Fein Uaill
interactiveMaps.alt: Regional map of Fein Uaill showing cities, a shard, the Titanwall, and the Gates of Aelthor
interactiveMaps.description: The regional map separates Fein Uaill from Zarathis and preserves a network of cities, fortifications, sacred sites, and monumental boundaries.

interactiveMaps.title: Voraketh
interactiveMaps.alt: Anky’s illustrated map of Voraketh, showing forests and mountains around a vast devastated interior
interactiveMaps.description: Anky’s angel-made map, known by 21 March 2026. The image preserves the island’s broad geography but does not label the Chains, Maw, Last Grove, Veiled Watch, or Temple of Secrets; their exact positions must not be inferred from appearance alone.

interactiveMaps.title: Eovar Harbor
interactiveMaps.alt: Map of Eovar Harbor showing a walled waterfront settlement, ships, and nearby farmland
interactiveMaps.description: The harbor’s form is its history: ships, walls, a compact waterfront, controlled approaches, and agricultural support beyond the urban core.

interactiveMaps.title: Babel-Ashur
interactiveMaps.alt: Full island map of Babel-Ashur dominated by wild biomes and a vast central crater
interactiveMaps.description: An island organized visually around a central wound. Its southern coast opens into the more detailed expedition geography of Greyward Littoral.

interactiveMaps.title: Luminar Spires
interactiveMaps.alt: Illustrated regional map of the Luminar Spires on Babel-Ashur’s coast
interactiveMaps.description: A dedicated regional map showing the crystal-tipped coastal formations and their surrounding terrain. Only the Luminar Spires label is treated as a confirmed named location; nearby features remain visually preserved but unnamed.

interactiveMaps.title: Greyward Littoral
interactiveMaps.alt: Annotated expedition map of Greyward Littoral on Babel-Ashur’s southern coast
interactiveMaps.description: The most operational map in the archive: it marks arrival, routes, refuge, resources, caverns, ruins, and hazardous wetlands.

questEventConsequences.Magnus quests beside Pristinia’s adventu: The scene establishes that the people Magnus later fights are companions rather than abstractions. His curiosity, appetite for useful objects, and preference for letting a better-positioned speaker handle Papirak are recognizable early traits, but nothing in the recovered expedition yet proves Rahu allegiance or hostility toward Pristinia.
questEventConsequences.Magnus becomes a Rahu information source: The transition matters because political criticism becomes operational usefulness. Sophina still limits his access and warns him not to overstep, so Magnus is not yet shown as a Rahu decision-maker; what is established is that he actively cultivates the relationship and supplies information favorable to Rahu interests.
questEventConsequences.Magnus fights Pristinia for the Rahu: His hidden bridge warning keeps the event from becoming a simple story of vanished feeling. Magnus chooses the attacking faction and endangers former companions while still trying to spare some of them from one trap. The alleged wall sabotage remains Paco’s contemporary testimony rather than a directly recovered action.
questEventConsequences.Magnus falls and returns during the Rahu: The return becomes the first major gap in a resurrection history that later defines Magnus. Later accounts connect his repeated returns to Rahu, Death, and Aria, but the present evidence does not assign a precise patron, rite, or mechanism to the interval between this fall and his reappearance.
questEventConsequences.The Rahu siege grinds against Pristinia: The continuing bombardment shows that the war was not one decisive clash. Siege engines, disease-bearing bodies, fire, structural damage, and deteriorating morale turn survival into civic labor, placing builders and responders such as the Ale-Chemy Knights inside the same history as battlefield champions.
questEventConsequences.Magnus abducts Melian for the Rahu: This mission establishes Magnus as an operational leader rather than a sympathetic outsider or ordinary combatant. The no-witness order directly creates the circumstances of Herb’s and Lilian’s deaths; Herb’s later restoration does not erase the choice, the violence, or Lilian’s loss.
questEventConsequences.Pristinia reconstructs Melian’s abductio: The physical evidence narrows what the town can responsibly claim: Melian was incapacitated, violence occurred, and the attackers possessed a route past the defenses. The investigation does not by itself reveal every participant or mechanism, preserving the difference between what witnesses know and what the broader archive can reconstruct.
questEventConsequences.Minerva finds no readable trace in Papir: The failed observation remains evidence rather than an embarrassment to be erased. Fredrick had also seen inscribed covers and blank pages, so Minerva’s result preserves the conditions under which capable investigators could honestly find nothing; it does not prove that the book was empty, substituted, or knowingly concealed.
questEventConsequences.Truesight reveals the grimoire’s hidden: The revelation changes the mystery’s world state instead of awarding retroactive progress. A new perceptual condition makes existing information visible, narrowing the question from whether the pages contain anything to why the writing was hidden, who knew how to reveal it, and what responsibilities follow from that knowledge.
questEventConsequences.Pell prepares Papirak’s burial and memor: The work makes memory material through a grave, a possible mausoleum, and the ordinary problem of paying for both. Pell’s damaged memory gives the labor additional weight: a person struggling to preserve parts of their own past is nevertheless helping a community preserve Papirak’s place in its history.
questEventConsequences.Pristinia opens a vote on Papirak’s Staf: The process distinguishes value from authority. Camilla identifies what a sale might fund, Melian argues that personal belonging should outweigh price, and several residents propose trusted custodians without treating magical capability as ownership. The funeral later resolves the immediate disposition when Scribonia refuses the staff and Melian orders it buried with Papirak.
questEventConsequences.Pristinia carries Papirak to his hill: The procession makes Papirak’s death civic history rather than a private loss. The Rite of the Flame asks the living to carry what the dead can no longer bear, while the road, statue, Training Dungeon, rain, music, and assembled townspeople turn Pristinia’s landscape into an active memorial. Pappy’s later claims about an older shared history remain attributed speech, not retroactive fact.
questEventConsequences.Papirak’s staff is entombed under Seques: The burial converts a debate about wealth and utility into a decision about provenance and stewardship. Fenwick’s spell protects the chosen disposition without granting him ownership; Camilla’s failed detection accurately records the spell’s effect but not her conclusion that theft occurred. The resulting mistrust becomes a continuing social consequence even though the object remains in the tomb.
questEventConsequences.Papirak’s mourners turn toward living: The funeral creates obligations rather than closure. Scribonia’s promise to work on the Training Dungeon is real even though success is not established, Pell discovers meaning in service, and Camilla leaves with greater suspicion. Herb’s call to the Pilgrim’s Hearth lets celebration coexist with grief, returning the town to food, drink, music, and relationships without pretending the loss is finished.
questEventConsequences.The first Called arrive in Prima: The arrival establishes the pattern that defines the early campaign: strangers are placed together before they understand the Gate, the gods, or one another. Their first important act is not conquest but accepting that an unfinished settlement and its people are now part of their responsibility.
questEventConsequences.The newcomers scout beyond Pristinia: The patrol gives the new arrivals their first evidence that Prima is stranger than the settlement suggests. The enormous distant movement remains unidentified, while John’s severed branch demonstrates that even apparently ordinary natural objects may be sustained by relationships the party does not yet understand.
questEventConsequences.Melian gives the newcomers a town to imp: Melian frames Pristinia as work rather than a reward. The meeting turns a collection of summoned adventurers into potential residents by asking them to notice roads, food, medicine, defense, and the material needs of people who cannot solve every problem with magic.
questEventConsequences.Forgax follows the pillar only he can se: Because the pillar is visible only to Forgax, the expedition cannot treat sight as shared proof. The floating stones and ash create an early lesson in testimony: the company must decide whether to trust a companion’s perception when the world supplies no confirmation to anyone else.
questEventConsequences.A trapped route to Eovar is reopened: Clearing the route connects Pristinia’s survival to the wider coast and establishes Eovar as a reachable civic center rather than a distant name. The trap also warns that travel between settlements is contested, making every reopened road a political and economic achievement as well as an adventure.
questEventConsequences.The Weary Traveler sends a rescue party: The mission turns tavern conversation into obligation. Recovered weapons and armor become tools for bringing missing people home, beginning the Common Man’s long role as a place where rumors, civilian needs, and adventuring decisions become consequential action.
questEventConsequences.Pristinia organizes militia, medicine, a: The assignments show that Pristinia cannot be secured by combat alone. Melian distributes responsibility across public health, food, materials, and defense, creating an early civic model in which the adventurers’ usefulness depends on whether they can build systems that outlast a single fight.
questEventConsequences.The ritual-site assault is stopped: Stopping the gathering prevents an immediate attack, but the old ritual ground proves that threats already have roots in Prima’s landscape. The victory gives Pristinia time while leaving open who prepared the site, why the pale creatures were drawn there, and what other dormant structures surround the settlement.
questEventConsequences.The mine dead and the missing companions: Recovery matters as much as victory: the party returns bodies, identifies losses, and finds the people the Weary Traveler feared were gone. The mission gives the settlement something it can mourn and celebrate honestly instead of allowing the missing to disappear into an unnamed mine.
questEventConsequences.Pristinia celebrates rescue and resurrec: The feast holds triumph and cost in the same room. Resurrection does not erase the dead, the fear, or the labor of recovery; the Common Man becomes the place where the town gives those events a shared meaning and begins building collective memory.
questEventConsequences.Four volunteers answer the militia’s cal: These four are not simply preparing for another quest. By training residents, they begin transferring competence away from exceptional adventurers and toward the community itself, an important step in making Pristinia defensible when its heroes are absent, divided, or dead.
questEventConsequences.A fog expedition reveals a hidden watche: The watcher’s brief appearance changes the patrol from a difficult journey into evidence of surveillance. Cobble cannot identify the armored figure or its purpose, so the record preserves the observation without turning it into a solved conspiracy.
questEventConsequences.The adventurers drill Pristinia’s volunt: The controlled course converts individual combat experience into a public resource. Rolen and Carandolchanar’s supervision also establishes a chain of responsibility: training must prepare people for danger without treating inexperienced volunteers as expendable material.
questEventConsequences.A dying messenger brings Eovar’s warning: The message pulls Pristinia into Eovar’s crisis and ends with an enemy vessel destroyed, but the Compass remains a dangerous unresolved object. The order to destroy it implies knowledge the party does not possess and makes the pursuit’s apparent victory only the beginning of a larger problem.
questEventConsequences.Pristinia’s palisade and moat take shape: The work is ordinary, visible, and cumulative: cut timber, treated logs, earthworks, stakes, and watchtowers. These defenses later matter precisely because people built them before the worst attack arrived, turning preparation into one of the campaign’s clearest forms of foresight.
questEventConsequences.A forest expedition finds a dead priest’: The chamber offers no living witness and no easy explanation, only an overgrown room and human remains. Its restraint is important: the party learns that Prima contains abandoned histories whose meaning cannot be recovered merely by finding them.
questEventConsequences.Two blue-mist sigils are broken in the F: Holy energy makes the mist glitter and recede, and the company confirms that this part of the forest has been cleared rather than declaring the entire danger ended. Their exhausted return to Pristinia, accompanied by ghostly butterflies, leaves both a practical method—find the marked trees and destroy the sigils—and an unresolved question about who placed them.
questEventConsequences.The First Forest reclaims the quarry roa: The expedition proves that a useful road can vanish when civic work becomes intermittent. Reaching the frozen stream and surviving the wolves restores knowledge of the route for the moment, but it also ties Pristinia’s access to stone and construction material to continued travel, maintenance, and respect for a landscape that does not remain passive.
questEventConsequences.Pristinia makes a pact with the wolves: The agreement rejects extermination as the only answer to scarcity. Cigal becomes an intermediary between settlement and pack, tying the farm’s safety to Pristinia’s willingness to help when prey is scarce and making coexistence a continuing duty rather than a one-time success.
questEventConsequences.Seven glyphs open an underground city: The revealed city greatly expands the scale of the ruins beneath Prima. Its seven glyphs and purple illumination indicate deliberate design, while the active defenses show that whatever ended the settlement did not render all of its systems harmless.
questEventConsequences.A Flying Horror escapes with lost intell: The escape is recorded as a failure of coordination rather than softened into an inconclusive victory. The creature carries away information and denies the party answers, creating a consequence that may return to Pristinia long after the immediate encounter.
questEventConsequences.Pristinia holds after its allies abandon: The defense proves that the town’s preparations and remaining people can matter even when expected allies do not appear. It also leaves a social wound: survival does not answer why support failed, and the defenders must rebuild trust as well as damaged fortifications.
questEventConsequences.The mountain party survives the storm ca: The cave saves the group from exposure but cannot give them comfort or certainty. Their short, cold rest makes the landscape itself an antagonist and shows how quickly an expedition can become a survival problem before any enemy appears.
questEventConsequences.The Eovar epidemic is traced to the wate: The discovery changes the response from treating individual sufferers to confronting shared infrastructure. It makes clean water, quarantine, and sanitation matters of regional security, while implicating the city’s crowded districts and neglected systems rather than blaming the sick.
questEventConsequences.A celestial test reveals the Wyrm’s hung: The radiant trial ends without explaining who designed it or what standard the participants were judged against. What remains is the sensed hunger beyond the test, a warning that even a successful encounter can reveal a threat far larger than the people who survived it.
questEventConsequences.Symin falls beyond the Gate: Symin’s decision to answer the plea alone turns urgency into isolation, and the bark-covered dead deny the company even immediate possession of his body. His loss becomes a warning about rescue calls, ambushes, and the cost of acting without enough witnesses or support.
questEventConsequences.The Narrows reveals Eovar’s sanitation f: The canal makes the epidemic’s cause materially visible: waste and drinking water occupy the same civic space. The party’s discovery exposes how poverty and neglected infrastructure can kill as effectively as monsters, forcing Eovar’s crisis into the realm of policy and public works.
questEventConsequences.The mountain-pass party clears an undead: Wren’s guidance prevents the group from entering a valley vulnerable to flooding, showing that judgment can be as important as strength. Surviving the undead attack then opens the route to the waiting host, converting caution into forward progress rather than retreat.
questEventConsequences.Pristinia adopts merchant penalties by t: The narrow 31–29 result preserves genuine disagreement inside the town. The vote matters because it subjects merchants to public consequence and shows Pristinia attempting to govern through debate and recorded decisions instead of letting wealth or adventuring power decide by default.
questEventConsequences.Two captured doppelgangers are sent home: The party survives the captives’ psychic resistance without choosing execution. Nienna’s sense that the pair arrived alive makes the banishment an act of difficult mercy and establishes that returning an enemy home can sometimes serve safety better than killing them.
questEventConsequences.The walking dead reach Pristinia’s appro: The horde is defeated, but the dead leave contaminated ground and a practical question about disposal. The aftermath refuses the clean ending of a battlefield victory: bodies, necrotic residue, and frightened residents still require labor after the fighting stops.
questEventConsequences.A reality-splitting ritual is foiled: The rival beacons and Quake’s staff provide enough evidence to stop the ritual but not enough to understand its full design. Destroying the site prevents the immediate rupture while burying clues, forcing later investigators to work from fragments instead of a complete explanation.
questEventConsequences.The meteor orb opens after the spider fa: Saray’s shot ends the immediate threat, but the opening orb replaces danger with uncertainty. The party has won access to an object of unknown origin and purpose, making curiosity, containment, and the decision to interact with it the next stage of the event.
questEventConsequences.Passage is secured toward the Thundering: The lifted quarantine restores Eovar’s harbor as a route rather than a boundary. Securing a ship turns the distant beacon into a reachable objective and ties the coming expedition to sailors, supplies, weather, and the cooperation of a city still recovering from disease.
questEventConsequences.Nienna is found bound in a forest cleari: The Dimensional Shackles make Nienna’s captivity more than a physical restraint and demonstrate that her captors planned for magical escape. The dead body and surrounding figures leave a violent scene whose motive must be reconstructed while the rescuers first decide how to get her free.
questEventConsequences.A landslide exposes the four-pillar ruin: Fernir’s death and the newly opened chamber bind discovery to cost. Mapping the geometric pillars and recovering journals give the party evidence, but the landslide also warns that the archive they seek is embedded in unstable terrain and incomplete lives.
questEventConsequences.A sea expedition discovers a new island: The keelboat journey expands the known geography beyond established routes. Reaching the high platform requires physical cooperation after threading dangerous cliffs, so the discovery is not merely a point on a map but proof that the party can make the passage again.
questEventConsequences.The Before’s distress call proves to be: The mimicry weaponizes the party’s willingness to answer familiar voices. Escaping into daylight preserves their lives but leaves the hidden caller active, making future rescue signals harder to trust and turning communication itself into contested terrain.
questEventConsequences.Rehevä’s cliffside dragon nest is cleare: The rope descent and battle remove a direct threat beneath the town, while Mayor Jovaz’s celebration makes the result publicly legible. Rehevä’s gratitude also gives the adventurers a regional relationship that extends beyond Pristinia’s immediate needs.
questEventConsequences.Nienna’s condemned sailors return to ser: The sailors begin the scene awaiting death as mutineers and end it provisioning Nienna’s ship. Their return to service preserves people and practical knowledge that execution would have destroyed, while leaving the history of the mutiny as part of the crew’s future trust.
questEventConsequences.The party breaks the harbor blockade: Acting through heavy rain, the company turns reconnaissance into a breach of the blockade and follows Huoth into a magically charged tower. The harbor opens, but Huoth’s role and the tower’s power carry the conflict beyond the ships and bridge.
questEventConsequences.The colossal archway’s false floor is fo: The probing spear discovers the trap before a person falls through it. The flickering square establishes that the structure manipulates perception, rewarding slow testing and making every apparently solid surface beyond the archway suspect.
questEventConsequences.The Rahu open their Pristinia enclave: The enclave brings a disciplined nocturnal institution into the settlement and gives the Rahu a permanent civic presence. Its violet altar-like focus is observed without a settled explanation, preserving both the opportunity for diplomacy and the unease surrounding unfamiliar power.
questEventConsequences.The screaming dungeon’s blood altar is c: Following the screams brings the party to a chamber whose horror is both physical and personal. When the blood boils away and a voice singles out Alyhotep, cleansing the altar becomes the beginning of a threat directed at a specific adventurer rather than the end of the dungeon’s danger.
questEventConsequences.Pristinia’s quarry corridor is stabilize: Sylvaaran’s seamless brace answers workers’ fear with a material repair, protecting both lives and the stone supply needed for the settlement’s growth. The event shows adventuring magic used as infrastructure rather than spectacle.
questEventConsequences.Water guardians emerge in the sector dun: Saturnia’s interference with the room’s water triggers four elemental defenders, revealing that the dungeon reacts to intrusion through systems as well as creatures. The encounter makes the party’s method of investigation part of the danger it produces.
questEventConsequences.The lich’s lair collapses: The slain lich and ruined lair end one immediate threat, but the undead woman and Melian’s refusal to admit her into town create a harder question about safety and personhood. Victory outside the portal does not settle who may belong inside Pristinia.
questEventConsequences.Rehevä forgets an unseen act of heroism: The party protects people who never learn what was done for them because the arcane displacement tears the witnesses and rescuers apart. The event preserves heroism without recognition and demonstrates how magical disruption can erase public memory without erasing the deed itself.
questEventConsequences.The dungeon survivors return to a mayor’: The mayor’s surprise confirms that the town had already accepted the party as dead. Their return converts presumed loss into celebration and reward, but it also records how completely the dungeon severed communication with those waiting outside.
questEventConsequences.Gudlaug and Beefy Boy win the race: The dangerous race gives the public a rare event measured by skill, endurance, and celebration rather than catastrophe. Gudlaug’s victory becomes communal memory and shows that the world’s history includes joy and spectacle alongside sacrifice.
questEventConsequences.Pristinia’s townsfolk openly support the: Residents arrive with tools because they still believe the adventurers’ work can improve the town. Ending the day with Melian’s practical instruction places trust beside labor: support is offered, but the heroes are still expected to learn how to build responsibly.
questEventConsequences.The Azarian Peaks expedition reaches the: Liora’s research carries the party across the sea and into an environment saturated with danger and magic. The glowing dead creature suggests that the Peaks alter even what no longer lives, deepening the expedition’s mystery without explaining the prophecy that led them there.
questEventConsequences.Jiangshi’s coffin reaches Gael’s shore: The landing is a recovery operation rather than a triumphant arrival. Adelia carrying the weakened Jiangshi from the water and the sailors handling the coffin show a group protecting both the living person before them and the unresolved meaning of what they have transported.
questEventConsequences.The worm hunt traps the party undergroun: Following Scout Lilian’s evidence leads to a collapse that turns investigators into trapped survivors. The faint haze inside the sealed cave raises the stakes: escape must happen before exhaustion and possible contamination make the original worm sightings irrelevant.
questEventConsequences.The corruption cave leaves its explorers: The party exits with recognizable bodies but not with confidence that the encounter ended at the cave mouth. Their shared sense of being followed turns survival into psychological and possibly supernatural uncertainty, an outcome that cannot be measured by wounds alone.
questEventConsequences.Wrath drives the tomb expedition toward: The blows outside and the ravens overhead show that Wrath can pressure the party without entering the tomb. With the company already wounded, continuing becomes a test of judgment: completing the objective must be weighed against giving Wrath more people to destroy.
questEventConsequences.The cave-trapped party digs free with a: Hours of excavation turn escape into collective endurance rather than a single spell or attack. Arjahn’s recovered fragments and the wave he feels preserve evidence of possible contamination, ensuring that freedom from the cave does not end the need for observation.
questEventConsequences.Delerium fragments rain outside Pristini: The explosion transforms the field beyond the wall into a contamination zone and leaves a haze-born spectre still at large. Recovering fragments may offer evidence, but every piece is also a hazard that threatens the people and defenses the adventurers are trying to protect.
questEventConsequences.The Gael tomb mission escapes through th: Quake’s crown and command activate the statues at the moment ordinary exits are no longer safe. The revealed tunnel lets the party finish the mission without accepting annihilation, making retreat a completed objective rather than a failure of courage.
questEventConsequences.Moirah returns with Jiangshi at a cost: Moirah’s diminished condition makes the recovery visibly costly even though the unseen struggle remains unknown. Elenia’s magic restores the goddess enough to continue, reversing the usual direction of divine aid and showing mortals supporting a wounded divine power.
questEventConsequences.Pristinia debates gold, business, and pu: The council forces the adventurers’ wealth into a civic argument: who benefits from new construction, which businesses deserve support, and how ordinary residents participate in growth. Offering gold does not settle those questions; it makes the need for accountable decisions more urgent.
questEventConsequences.The Gael mechanism drains nearby magic: The wheel removes access to the Weave from everyone nearby, turning a successful activation into an immediate loss of capability. Because the effect later settles, the party gains a dangerous piece of evidence about the ruins without learning who built the mechanism or what it was meant to power.
questEventConsequences.Melian places Pristinia among neighborin: The briefing makes clear that Pristinia’s apparent smallness is not isolation. Its survival depends on diplomacy, roads, nearby settlements, and the older dangers around it; every later civic decision occurs inside that regional web.
questEventConsequences.Eovar’s fire makes rebuilding a regional: The request for workers turns another settlement’s disaster into a shared labor problem. It establishes an early precedent for Pristinia and Eovar affecting one another through people and infrastructure rather than existing as self-contained quest locations.
questEventConsequences.Pristinia’s cedar is stolen in Eovar: The theft converts a decorative construction choice into regional consequence. Protecting the successor to the Common Man now depends on Eovar’s trade and underworld, while the adventurers must weigh recovery against the cost of damaging Pristinia’s reputation.
questEventConsequences.Eovar’s sailors refuse the sea: Because shipping is Eovar’s organizing function, fear at the docks threatens food, movement, work, and every settlement relying on the harbor. The unanswered question is not only what happened at sea, but how long a port can remain itself without sailing.
questEventConsequences.Arjahn warns that no one controls all of: The warning disciplines every later expedition: a guide can know part of the ruin without owning it, and a faction can occupy chambers without controlling the systems around them. Uncertainty becomes operational knowledge rather than an invitation to invent certainty.
questEventConsequences.The gas geyser field tests Gael’s travel: The choice turns geography into a party-level decision with costs on both sides. The bones show that the hazard predates the travelers, while the failed navigation makes their route part of the event rather than mere transition between encounters.
questEventConsequences.Prior knowledge changes the second geyse: The return proves that exploration can create durable advantage without conquering a place. Recognition, route planning, sampling, and prediction are all consequences of memory, and future parties inherit a location instead of a reset encounter.
questEventConsequences.Travelers reach Larkhollow and open it t: Opening Larkhollow for continued life changes the meaning of arrival. The party does not merely complete a journey; it adds a settlement to the world’s repeatable social geography, where later relationships can accumulate beyond the originating quest.
questEventConsequences.Relics tie Larkhollow to its ruined towe: The relics make the tower more than scenery without settling its explanation. They provide a material question future stories can answer while preserving the difference between evidence of an older history and a finished account of that history.
questEventConsequences.Gael’s coast becomes a route toward Lark: A repeatable route turns separate names into a connected travel network. Gael now functions as a departure point, Verdelune as a passage, and Larkhollow as a destination whose accessibility can shape future movement and trade.
questEventConsequences.The new vanguard entrusts leadership to: Peer trust and martial competence are both tested; the contest does not by itself finalize the appointment.
questEventConsequences.Severina turns the new vanguard into an: The new vanguard gains the logistical shape needed to operate as a lasting faction rather than an improvised quest party. The exact naming day remains unrecovered, and participation in the founding discussion does not automatically prove lifelong membership, but the company now has continuity beyond a single meeting.
questEventConsequences.The Veilguard name enters the public rec: The name gives other people a faction they can recognize and a standard against which its conduct can be judged. It also establishes the Veilguard as separate from both the earlier Vanguard and the Ale-Chemy Knights without denying that their operations and relationships may overlap.
questEventConsequences.The Veilguard prepares to recover Thorn: The attempt to bring Thorn home becomes the first major test of whether the Veilguard’s language of mutual protection survives catastrophe. A member is not reduced to equipment, intelligence, or acceptable loss, while the missing steps of the operation and Thorn’s later return remain unresolved.
questEventConsequences.Thorn returns and names the Veilguard as: Thorn’s own words confirm the Veilguard as a lived community rather than only Severina’s organizational theory. The mechanism of her return, the cult ritual’s outcome, and the full recovery company remain open instead of being converted into invented certainty.
questEventConsequences.Magnus returns and Hope withers: Moirah reveals that restoring Magnus required retrieving a soul Death owns, while Dumuzi's gift gives Magnus a death-working power capable of affecting Tree Shards. Hope begins to wither as Adelia and Jiangshi try to save her. Adelia's self-blame is preserved as her belief, not proof that she is responsible for Magnus's choice.
